fields.summary: Autonomous plan run for change set 01M6VY7 (Scheduling as policy), which follows decision workflows-are-the-rules. No owner took part. The planner read the daemon's candidate selection (daemonCandidates in internal/api/daemon.go skips every accepted change set that serves no milestone as SkipNoMilestone), the plan workflow's milestone-check step (internal/workflow/builtin/plan.toml, internal/api/run_milestone.go), the request --milestone plumbing and the plan guide. It raised four questions in one call: which milestone this change set serves, where the scheduling rule lives, which values it takes, and what milestone-check does once backlog work can ship. The arbiter answered with Decision scheduling-policy-shape. (1) Serve milestone-29 directly, with no new milestone. (2) The rule lives in a new checked-in .rhiza/policy.toml under [schedule], so every daemon reads the same rule, and a missing file or key means the default. (3) backlog = after (default) | before | skip, oldest accepted first inside the backlog; an unknown value is a rhiza check problem, and the daemon then skips backlog work with the bad value in the skip detail. (4) milestone-check stays. It fails only for a run started with --milestone whose change set does not serve that milestone, or when backlog is skip. The planner then wrote four leaves: the policy file and its check, the daemon's backlog picks, the relaxed milestone-check, and the plan guide's milestone wording.
fields.title: Scheduling as policy: autonomous plan interview (arbiter answers)
